stories.title: Mathematical modeling and statistical analysis for predicting success in intrauterine insemination, intracytoplasmic sperm injection, and frozen embryo transfer
stories.description: Infertility affects millions of couples worldwide, and assisted reproductive technologies (ART) such as intrauterine insemination (IUI), intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI), and frozen embryo transfer (ET Freeze) are commonly used to treat it. However, the success rates of these methods vary considerably, and the factors that predict successful outcomes are not fully understood. Identifying these predictors is crucial for personalized treatment planning and improving clinical decision-making. This study aims to identify and compare the significant predictors of treatment success across three ART methods: IUI, ICSI, and ET Freeze. We also seek to develop statistical and mathematical models to evaluate the relationship between patient-related factors and pregnancy outcomes, and to assess which model provides the best fit for predicting treatment success. This retrospective cohort study was conducted at Royan Institute, Tehran, Iran, using data from 2011–2014. The unit of analysis was the ART treatment cycle. After data cleaning, 6240 cycles remained. The final ordinal logistic regression analyses included 4592 cycles with a known ordinal outcome (blighted ovum, abortion, or live birth). Repeated cycles from the same couple were accounted for using generalized estimating equations (GEE) with couple ID as the clustering variable. Ordinal logistic regression was used to model the association between predictors and treatment outcome. Of the 6240 participants, 209 underwent IUI, 2598 underwent ICSI, and 1783 underwent ET Freeze. For IUI, significant predictors of reduced success were increasing age (OR 0.94, 95% CI 0.87–1.00, p < 0.058), BMI $$\ge $$ 30 kg/m$$^2$$ (OR 0.46, 95% CI 0.19–1.10, p $$=$$ 0.076), and longer duration of infertility (OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.86–1.02, p = 0.116). For ICSI, significant predictors included age (OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.92–0.95, p < 0.001), BMI $$\ge $$ 30 kg/m$$^2$$ (OR 0.74, 95% CI 0.58–0.95, p $$=$$ 0.018), fertilization rate (OR 1.73, 95% CI 1.21–2.50, p $$=$$ 0.003), number of mature oocytes (OR 2.31, 95% CI 1.41–3.83, p $$=$$ 0.001), and number of grade A embryos (OR 1.37, 95% CI 1.04–1.82, p $$=$$0.025). For ET Freeze, age (OR 0.97, 95% CI 0.95–0.99, p $$=$$ 0.002) and number of previous abortions (OR 0.77, 95% CI 0.60–0.99, p $$=$$ 0.037) were significant negative predictors of success. The predictors of treatment success differ significantly across the three ART methods. For IUI, BMI, duration of infertility, and age were the main predictors. For ICSI, a broader set of factors including BMI, age, number of embryos, fertilization rate, and PCOS were influential. For ET Freeze, only age and number of previous abortions were significant. These findings highlight the importance of patient-specific factors in ART outcomes and suggest that tailored treatment strategies based on individual predictors may improve success rates. The proposed statistical and mathematical models provide valuable tools for clinicians to better counsel patients and optimize treatment selection.

stories.title: L’Oréal Groupe Honours Four Thai Researchers in 24th 'For Women in Science' Programme
stories.description: Bangkok, 6 November 2026 – L’Oréal Groupe in Thailand, a global leader in beauty, continues to champion the role of women researchers in science for its 24th consecutive year by awarding research fellowships worth 250,000 THB each and honorary plaques to four outstanding female researchers under the L’Oréal Thailand “For Women in Science” Fellowship Programme for 2026. This year marks the first time the programme has expanded the applicant age limit from 40 to 45 years old, broadening opportunities for female researchers to present high-potential research. Selected from more than 89 research submissions, the programme aims to recognise and empower women researchers while inspiring the next generation of young women in science who play a vital role in driving Thailand’s scientific progress in the fields of environment, health, and sustainability. This reflects L’Oréal’s purpose to “Create the Beauty that Moves the World,” supporting research and development with the potential to generate positive impact for society, while raising wider awareness of the achievements of Thai women researchers.
